speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) what is the current adoption rate of outcome-based contracting (OBC) for public sector security service buyers; (b) whether the Ministry tracks the adoption rate for private sector security service buyers; (c) whether these adoption rates have met the Ministry’s targets; and (d) what is the plan to further increase the adoption rate of OBC in the public and private sectors.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether the Ministry is promoting the adoption of outcome-based contracting for the procurement of security services by managing agents appointed by annually-elected MCST Councils, given that short contracting periods remain a key impediment to the adoption of technologically-enabled security solutions at private residential estates; and (b) if so, what more can be done to further promote this.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: It will enable security agencies to innovate and deliver more productive solutions that integrate manpower, technology and process improvements.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: OBC offers the potential for buyers to achieve better security outcomes at lower long-term costs, in particular, for manpower.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: The remaining agencies will come on board over the next few years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Hence, we can expect the adoption rate to increase in the coming years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: MHA will continue to work closely with industry partners in the engagement and training of buyers to assist them in their transition to OBC.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: This includes firms providing managing agent services to Management Corporation Strata Title (MCST) councils of private residences.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: More case studies and examples will, gradually, be included in due course.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: In addition, MHA will continue supporting concurrent engagement initiatives by industry associations and the union, where experiences and best practices on OBC are shared.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: We also commend the various ground-up efforts to better facilitate adoption of OBC, such as the Association of Certified Security Agencies', or ACSAs', Step-by-Step Guide launched last year and the Security Associations Singapore's development of an online outcome-based tender generator and repository.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: These are encouraging efforts that we will continue to work with our partners to ensure higher adoption of OBC.
